tool_args.old_string: The central result is negative: \textbf{all auxiliary spatial head configurations perform at or below the Vanilla baseline} on Collision Avoidance Rate. Auxiliary spatial supervision does not improve VLA collision avoidance under any of the twelve configurations tested. Preliminary v2 factorial data from the $2{\times}2$ subset reveal an ordinal interaction between gradient flow and normalization. Gradient flow through the auxiliary head into the vision encoders is detrimental to safety ($\Delta = -4.2$\,pp within the BatchNorm conditions), and BatchNorm amplifies this damage compared to LayerNorm. The BatchNorm + gradient flow cell (Full OCC) is both the worst-performing and the most unstable configuration, with cross-seed standard deviation of 0.064, nearly three times that of the other three factorial cells. Spatial label content does not affect outcomes: Full OCC (ground-truth occupancy), Random OCC (random binary labels), and Depth (egocentric depth maps) all fall within cross-seed variance of each other and of the Vanilla baseline. The spatial information itself, whether structured or random, is irrelevant to safety; the gradient pathway and normalization dynamics determine the outcome.
tool_args.new_string: The central finding is a statistically significant \textbf{crossover interaction between normalization type and gradient flow} ($p{=}0.025$, 7.3\,pp interaction effect). BatchNorm with gradient flow (Full OCC) achieves the highest Collision Avoidance Rate (0.797, $+$1.7\,pp above Vanilla), while LayerNorm with gradient flow (Full OCC+LN) produces the worst safety behavior (0.743, $-$3.7\,pp below Vanilla), despite preserving pretrained representations. Removing gradient flow under BatchNorm causes catastrophic degradation (Detach OCC, 0.746, $-$3.4\,pp, $p{=}0.031$), the only statistically significant pairwise difference. Gradient flow benefits are thus BatchNorm-mediated, not an intrinsic property of auxiliary gradients. Spatial label content does not affect outcomes: Full OCC (ground-truth occupancy), Random OCC (random binary labels), and Depth (egocentric depth maps) all fall within cross-seed variance of each other when gradient flow is maintained. The spatial information itself, whether structured or random, is irrelevant to safety; the normalization--gradient-flow interaction determines the outcome.
